html:
Singapura was a Malay trading kingdom on the island of Singapore in the 14th century. Its founding is told in the Malay Annals, which say a prince of Palembang, Sang Nila Utama, named it the Lion City.

Digs on Fort Canning Hill and by the river have found Chinese porcelain, coins and gold, showing a busy port. Older records call it Temasek. It sat between the powers of Java and Siam.

At the end of the 14th century it was attacked, and its last ruler fled to found Malacca; he is usually identified with Parameswara. The island then stayed a small outpost until the founding of modern Singapore in 1819.
sum: Singapura was a Malay trading kingdom on the island of Singapore in the 14th century. Its founding is told in the Malay Annals, which say a prince of Palembang, Sang Nila Utama, named it the Lion City.
